{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to counteract overconfidence.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if recent history shows mean reversion (last 5-7 days trending downward).",
    "Increase forecast lag by 1-2 days if sentiment is bullish (sentiment > 0.25) to avoid overshoot after spikes.",
    "Apply upward bias correction if sentiment is strongly bullish (sentiment > 0.50) and true outcome is below forecast — model may be overreacting to sentiment.",
    "Use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment is positive, apply 10% upward bias; if negative, apply 10% downward bias to forecast mean.",
    "Avoid overfitting to recent highs: if last 3-5 days show sharp upward moves, cap forecast growth to 3-5% per day to prevent overshoot.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 10-15% to align with mean reversion behavior.",
    "For sentiment = 0.00, use 30-day moving average as baseline to avoid sentiment-driven noise."
  ]
}
